title: Danger actions keep the vivid destructive red; away data and error states take a muted red
context: Once error colours stopped reusing brand coral, one red had to serve both badges and rows that carry text and buttons that confirm a destructive action. A vivid red clashes with the muted teal and court palette on dense surfaces, yet a muted red is too weak on a danger button.
decision: `--destructive` stays shadcn's danger-action colour, a vivid red, hsl(13 85% 42%) (4.83:1 against its near-white foreground), used by the Button `destructive` variant, with `--destructive-text` for danger-zone headings on cards. `--away` is a muted coral-red, hsl(13 60% 40%) (5.63:1), for opponent and loss data: the away set tally, score border and figures, the rally lose marker and the move buttons for lost points, with `--away-text` for their text and icons on cards. `--error` is the same muted red for error states, with `--error-text` for error text on cards: alerts, toasts, failed-write rings and form messages.

alternatives.option: One vivid red for every destructive surface
alternatives.reason: Clashes with the muted teal and court palette on badges and rows.

alternatives.option: One muted red for every destructive surface
alternatives.reason: Too weak on a button that confirms a destructive action.

consequences: A destructive action takes --destructive; opponent or loss data takes --away; an error state takes --error.
Away and error share a value today but are separate tokens, so either can change on its own.
